It's Risk of Rain 1, but Risk of Rain-ier. 10/10
No seriously though, it's great. The art is gorgeous. It feels more stable, it plays fantastically. There's QoL things and items from RoR2 that improve on the original game in a fantastic way. There's rebalancing of all sorts, in both nerfs *and* buffs that are perfectly necessary and warranted. It's somehow the hardest iteration of the series and that's GREAT because even RoR2 was too easy once you got into the right groove, unless you deliberately played on Monsoon with ONLY the negative artifacts. It's the kind of remake and remaster that we needed.

A perfect example of a remaster done right. Risk of Rain Returns manages to be an amazing upgrade over the great, but somewhat flawed original Risk of Rain that came out a decade ago. The most important thing it fixes is the way multiplayer works. You can finally play with your friends without needing to use an external program like Hamachi. The multiplayer now works through Steam, which makes hosting games with friends way easier.
Other than that, it also adds a bunch of content without straying too far from the original. The music is, of course, amazing, the new art style looks way better too but the controls are still tight. A minor gripe I do have with Risk of Rain Returns is that fall damage can be a bit of a pain in the ass sometime, especially with how much verticality some of the maps have. 
All in all, Risk of Rain Returns is IMO perfect for both veterans that played the original game and newcomers to Risk of Rain.

Some people have complained about the strafing mechanic and i think that its fine. What isn't fine however, is that some achievements only unlock for the lobby leader. Also items are automatically picked up which makes it very hard for the right people to get the right items in a multiplayer setting. Also mob spawns are very arbitrary. It can spawn a whole legion on one player while leaving another without anything to do. Overall, the multiplayer makes me want to play alone. In every way you could interact with other players, its negative. The only exception being you can both kill things but that hardly makes up for item pickups being stolen. (and yes i was playing with item sharing forced barely helped). Like why doesnt it make a separate instanced chests for each player? Or hell why not make it so whenever you pick up an item it gives a copy to each other player? (excluding printers and the like whenever they're added). Even if you had to make the chests cost 4 times as much. At the very least a mini-map that is filled in as you go showing what has and hasnt been grabbed by you or team.

There is little to no mobility in the game, at base (why arent goat hoof and feather unlocked from the get go), making the platforming taxing. You cant even drop through platforms manually. Miss one jump and you have to waste almost a minute to walk back over climb back up and reattempt. Not that the platforming is particularly difficult but it feels like its just not what should be the focus. And with all the random platforms and free falls, WHY IS THERE FALL DAMAGE?! It just feels completely out of place IMO. Also with the lack of mobility some attacks are just straight up unavoidable or they are only avoidable with 1 of your cooldowns typically which doesnt come back up fast enough to dodge the next attack in most cases.

Please let us ban some items from dropping. like for every 20 items in the pool you can eliminate 1 or something. I feel cheated every time voltaic mitt spawns, especially because I completed a trial to unlock it and now it plagues my every waking moment. its the most useless item and ive had it drop in multiples on stage 1 to the point where it made up half my inventory of 6 items.

Why is artificer just so bad? His basic attack is in my opinion the worst in the game and you cant even replace it with a providence trial. Having his hover from ror2 would be really nice for him.

Loader is incredibly awkward. The grapple hook is just too fast to consistently be able to cancel it when you want to use the momentum. Also his basic attack caused my RSI to act up within 3 stages just have it be hold to combo. Or if i do have to press it repeatedly i should be able to turn around mid combo.

Enforcer would be a lot better if his entire gameplan wasnt made completely irrelevant by 2 of the 4 elite types, blue and orange. Why can the missles go through walls and hit you from behind? "Use protect and serve against a wall to prevent yourself from being flanked" Good way to die IMO.

And then there is engineer, easily the best character in the game (although an argument could be made for huntress). From the fire and forget missles to the turrets to his basic attack which still hits enemies while jumping to dodge things, he makes playing the rest of the cast feel like a joke.

another petty thing, its not possible to invite people solely with controller you have to use your mouse to click invite so i would argue it doesnt have full controller support. 

Will update review upon further updates to the game, but so far its a no from me chief.

This game is incredibly fun and challenging, and the Providence Trials added in Returns take away so much unnecessary grinding to unlock new abilities and items. I absolutely love this game and will continue to do so. 
However, I do have a few complaints. I feel that some maps are a bit too large for the player to navigate in a reasonable amount of time. Teleporter spawns can be hidden in a corner of a map and can take players 5-8 minutes to find, which will make the game more difficult the longer it takes to find it. I think that a particle system similar to Risk of Rain 2's would be extremely helpful. While the particles are still present, they cover much less distance from the teleporter than Risk of Rain 2, which combined with the 2D perspective, make the teleporter far more difficult to find. Either the teleporter should be easier to find, or our characters should be faster, I think. 
I believe that a tweak to the controls would also greatly benefit the playerbase. It's a little awkward to turn around with A or D to face an enemy before shooting them. I think it would be beneficial if the player fired which direction their mouse was facing, not their character. They would still move slow while firing of course, I'm not asking them to make every character Huntress.
 PS: ♥♥♥♥ flying enemies.
 PSS: Hopoo is very good with post-launch updates and balance changes so I wouldn't be surprised if my criticism is addressed in the future.

Fun, but several complaints.

1) Controls are awful. If using mouse+keyboard input settings, characters should ALWAYS face the direction of the cursor (Bandit, Commando, Pilot) rather than the direction they last moved while firing. Additionally, Loader is completely unplayable because tether angling relies on what combination of ASDW directional inputs are pressed at the same time as SHIFT (what?). Her grapple should travel in the direction of the cursor, and she should stick to surfaces until SHIFT is released like in RoR2. In my many runs of Loader, pressing SHIFT gets me killed most of the time unless I somehow got Hardlight Afterburner.

2) If playing Fullscreen, using mouse+keyboard controls, and if your system has multiple monitors, your mouse is not locked to the window your game is occupying. This effectively allows you to click out of the game and lose control of your character until you tab back into the game. This unfortunately happened to me in a run where I was in the last stage of final boss and died because I clicked out of my game. This point is not really a concern for players not using mouse+keyboard with multiple monitors, but it's a hilariously terrible oversight in my opinion.

3) Scaling is pretty bad between difficulties, and it does not feel like this game was play tested. Drizzle is quite possibly the only playable mode in Co-op. In 1P, you can play Rainstorm if you tweak the amount of damage your character deals/takes and play at a pace of 3-4 minutes per stage or play slower than that and just get unbelievably lucky on what items you roll. (Maybe I just need to get good?).

4) If maps weren't gigantic or players have some indication of what direction the teleporter is from spawn, you wouldn't waste so much time just looking for it. In RoR2, you pretty much know from spawn where the teleporter is based on particle effects, so time isn't quite as precious. In RoRR, though, you have to hunt down the teleporter immediately and charge it ASAP. Items and character progression are secondary. If you prioritize findings items and getting your build online, you just get outscaled in later stages. Bad game design due to gigantic maps.

Risk of Rain Returns is fun to play, but I will not recommend others buy this game until the developers balance some input systems and astronomical differences between difficulties. Just play RoR2, don't buy this game.
